says: One person founds two Teams that are both named 'Platform' (team.found twice: two ids) and commits one instructions source to each. Earlier work runs in Team A: a start composed over Team A, selected, activated in a Claude Code session, and that conversation opened as a recipient link scoped to Team A. The launcher (surface.drive) lists both Teams by name with a short id apart, Team A selected because the existing recipient is bound to it. Down and Enter browse Team B: browse_scope becomes Team B while selected_scope stays Team A and the recipient link stays the same; only Space explicitly selects Team B's instructions, and then selected_scope is Team B. Tab and Enter dispatch one new start whose preparation.compose basis is Team B alone; route.select records Team B's route for that request. Negative: the two Teams are never merged — every scope, route and request names one id; browsing Team B changes neither the selection nor the existing conversation, which stays linked to Team A; the Team B start carries nothing of Team A's source or history; the repository location selects no Team; and a selection naming the Team by its shared name instead of a route id is refused at admission (pattern_mismatch /selected).
